hook: Tianqi Chen built his reputation as a graduate student by creating tools that made machine learning systems faster and easier to deploy at scale. He earned bachelor's and master's degrees from Shanghai Jiao Tong University before completing a PhD at the University of Washington's Paul G. Allen School in 2019, advised by Carlos Guestrin. During his PhD he created XGBoost, a gradient boosting library that became a default choice for structured data problems in industry and machine learning competitions, and he co-created Apache MXNet, an early deep learning framework, and Apache TVM, a compiler that lets deep learning models run efficiently across many kinds of hardware. In 2019 he co-founded OctoML, later renamed OctoAI, serving as its chief technologist to commercialize the machine learning compilation techniques behind TVM, and the company was acquired by NVIDIA in 2024. He is now an Associate Professor in the Machine Learning and Computer Science Departments at Carnegie Mellon University and a Distinguished Engineer at NVIDIA, and he continues to lead open source projects including MLC-LLM for deploying large language models on everyday devices.
name: Tianqi Chen
moniker: Associate Professor, Carnegie Mellon University, and Distinguished Engineer, NVIDIA

primary.name: Chen and Guestrin, XGBoost: A Scalable Tree Boosting System, arXiv
Chen et al., TVM: An Automated End-to-End Optimizing Compiler for Deep Learning, arXiv

timeline.event: Releases XGBoost as an open source project while a graduate student
timeline.impact: Introduces a scalable gradient boosting system that quickly becomes a standard tool for structured data problems

timeline.event: Publishes XGBoost: A Scalable Tree Boosting System with Carlos Guestrin
timeline.impact: Documents the algorithmic and systems techniques behind XGBoost, including sparsity aware learning and cache efficient tree construction

timeline.event: Publishes TVM: An Automated End-to-End Optimizing Compiler for Deep Learning with a team of coauthors
timeline.impact: Introduces a compiler stack that gives deep learning models performance portability across CPUs, GPUs, and emerging accelerators

timeline.event: Completes his PhD at the University of Washington and co-founds OctoML as Chief Technologist
timeline.impact: Moves from academic research into commercializing machine learning compilation technology

timeline.event: OctoAI, the renamed OctoML, is acquired by NVIDIA, and he becomes a Distinguished Engineer there
timeline.impact: Brings his compiler and deployment work into NVIDIA's platform while continuing his CMU faculty role

quick_facts: Created XGBoost, a gradient boosting library widely used in industry and machine learning competitions
Co-created Apache TVM, an open source compiler for running deep learning models across diverse hardware
Co-created Apache MXNet, one of the early widely adopted deep learning frameworks
Earned a PhD from the University of Washington's Paul G. Allen School in 2019, advised by Carlos Guestrin
Co-founded OctoML, later OctoAI, as Chief Technologist in 2019, acquired by NVIDIA in 2024
Associate Professor in the Machine Learning and Computer Science Departments at Carnegie Mellon University, and Distinguished Engineer at NVIDIA

achievements.title: XGBoost
achievements.impact: Became one of the most widely used machine learning libraries for structured data, powering many winning solutions in data science competitions and production systems across industry.

achievements.title: Apache TVM
achievements.impact: Gave developers an open source compiler that automatically optimizes deep learning models for CPUs, GPUs, and specialized accelerators, reducing the work needed to deploy models across different hardware.

achievements.title: Apache MXNet (co-creator)
achievements.impact: Helped establish one of the first deep learning frameworks built for both research flexibility and production scale, later adopted as an Apache Software Foundation project.

achievements.title: Co-founder and Chief Technologist, OctoML / OctoAI
achievements.impact: Turned his research on machine learning compilation into a company focused on automated model deployment, which NVIDIA acquired in 2024.

achievements.title: MLC-LLM
achievements.impact: Created an engine for compiling and running large language models efficiently on phones, laptops, and other consumer hardware.
